messages.content:
Risk: Attack on AI agents
Description: Attackers intentionally create vulnerabilities or exploit existing vulnerabilities in external resources (tools/database/applications/services/other agents) that AI agents rely on to execute their intended actions or to achieve their goals.
Concern: Compromised external resources could impact the AI agent's performance in different ways, such as manipulating AI agents to pursue a different goal, manipulating AI agents to execute undesired actions, capturing and relaying interactions between AI agents to malicious actors, and getting AI agents to share personal or confidential information.
Policy: Supply Chain & Geopolitical Risks

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0084.002: Activation Triggers - ATLAS — Adversaries may discover keywords or other triggers (such as incoming emails, documents being added, incoming message, or other workflows) that activate an agent and may cause it to run additional actions.

Understanding these triggers can reveal how the AI agent is activated and controlled. This may also expose additional paths for compromise, as an adversary could attempt to trigger the agent from outside its environment and drive it to perform unintended or malicious actions. [found by 2/2 queries]
  Siblings: Tool Definitions - ATLAS, Embedded Knowledge - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.TA0015: Lateral Movement - ATLAS — The adversary is trying to move through your AI environment.

Lateral Movement consists of techniques that adversaries may use to gain access to and control other systems or components in the environment. Adversaries may pivot towards AI Ops infrastructure such as model registries, experiment trackers, vector databases, notebooks, or training pipelines. As the adversary moves through the environment, they may discover means of accessing additional AI-related tools, services, or applications. AI agents may also be a valuable target as they commonly have more permissions than standard user accounts on the system. [found by 2/2 queries]
  Siblings: Command and Control - ATTACK Mobile, Defense Evasion - SPARTA, Lateral Movement - ATTACK Mobile
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0029: Denial of AI Service - ATLAS — Adversaries may target AI-enabled systems with a flood of requests for the purpose of degrading or shutting down the service.
Since many AI systems require significant amounts of specialized compute, they are often expensive bottlenecks that can become overloaded.
Adversaries can intentionally craft inputs that require heavy amounts of useless compute from the AI system. [found by 2/2 queries]
  Siblings: Evade AI Model - ATLAS, Spamming AI System with Chaff Data - ATLAS, Erode Dataset Integrity - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#Attacker: Attacker — An agent that attempts to exploit vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access to data or systems.
  Siblings: Non-Person Entity, User, Person
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#T0820: Exploitation for Evasion - ATTACK ICS — Adversaries may exploit a software vulnerability to take advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to evade detection. Vulnerabilities may exist in software that can be used to disable or circumvent security features.
  Siblings: Rootkit - ATTACK ICS, Spoof Reporting Message - ATTACK ICS, System Binary Proxy Execution - ATTACK ICS

axes.rationale: The risk explicitly mentions 'attackers', making 'Attacker' the most relevant class to represent the agent performing the attack.
The description mentions 'vulnerabilities' and 'exploiting existing vulnerabilities'. Activation triggers can be exploited to manipulate the AI agent, making it a relevant instrument for the attack.
